method.label: Find a base and perpendicular height

annotationRationale: The method finds vertices by intersecting lines, identifies the altitude using perpendicular slopes, and computes base and height with the distance formula before applying the triangle area formula.
sourceMethod: Follows the official primary solution using base AB and the altitude from (2,2) to (5,5), with the intersection calculations and perpendicularity made explicit.

review.mathCheck: Solving the line equations gives \(A=(6,4)\) and \(B=(4,6)\). The perpendicular foot is \(H=(5,5)\), on segment AB. Thus \(AB=2\sqrt2\), \(PH=3\sqrt2\), and the area is 6, choice C.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Originally worded, faithful adaptation of official solution 7's primary base-and-altitude method on page 3. The vertices and altitude agree with the page 4 figure, and the candidate explicitly reconstructs them without needing that figure.
review.annotationCheck: The assessed intersection, distance and triangle-area nodes match the calculations; point-slope form and perpendicular slopes are suitable support. A point-to-line distance-formula node is unnecessary.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The four exact links cover line equations, intersections, coordinate distances and triangle area. The partial slope link supports the finite-slope perpendicular test used here; vertical and coincident-line cases are not demonstrated.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: 8.G.B.8 supports coordinate distances, and G-GPE.B.7 partially supports the resulting triangle-area calculation. G-GPE.B.5 supports applying perpendicular slopes, without proving the criterion; writing the two supplied-slope equations alone does not evidence its special construction requirement. G-GPE.B.4's theorem-proof aspect is not demonstrated. 6.G.A.1 has formula-level overlap here, without its composing/decomposing method. No US link is supplied for intersections.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: All five selected nodes fit their assessed or supporting roles. The method uses endpoint distances after constructing the altitude, exactly as the annotations claim.
